process_area.title: Specialized Costing (Project, Service, Intercompany) & Cost Governance

fields.Participants: Trade/Government sales (VS-11/VS-46), Project Finance (VS-11.2), Procurement (VS-03), Controller
fields.Trigger: Project/contract award (VS-11/VS-46); project cost transaction; project close-out
fields.Volume: ~ Active B2B/G2G projects (VS-11.2/VS-46.2); ~30% trade + 10% corporate revenue

workflows.name: Project / Job Costing for B2B & Government Contracts

Automation Opportunity: - WBS-driven auto cost collection from AP/procurement/timesheet; real-time margin dashboard; close-out auto-reconciliation
Controls: - CTL-706: project cost collected to WBS; actual-vs-budget monitored weekly; final margin reconciled to revenue at close-out
Cross-references: - links to VS-11.2/VS-46.2 (project/government), W918/W162/W793 (margin/bid/close), W4632 (revenue match)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Cost-miss risk**: Project cost (subcontractor, freight to site) not captured to the WBS understates project cost and overstates project margin; mitigated by WBS-driven cost collection
- **Margin-erosion-blind risk**: Late margin detection prevents corrective action; mitigated by real-time actual-vs-budget monitoring (VS-11.2)
System Touchpoints: - Project/job module (VS-11.2); AP (VS-15); procurement (VS-03); GL (VS-17.1); revenue recognition (VS-157 W4632)

steps.activity: Set up the project/job cost structure (WBS): material by delivery stage, direct labor, subcontractor, equipment rental, freight to site, project overhead; define the cost-collection method (actual) and the revenue-matching method (W4632)
Collect actual project cost (material issues, AP invoices, timesheets, subcontractor bills, freight) to the project WBS; monitor actual-vs-budget margin (VS-11.2 W918) and flag margin erosion
At project close-out (VS-11.2 W793), compute final project cost and margin, reconcile to revenue recognized (W4632), and feed lessons-learned into future bid costing (VS-11.2 W162)

fields.Trigger: Service/installation sale (VS-12); service cost transaction; periodic refresh
fields.Volume: Installation & repair services (VS-12.1); tool rental; workshops

Automation Opportunity: - Loaded-labor-rate engine; timesheet-to-work-order auto-collection; service-margin dashboards
Controls: - CTL-706 (ensure controlled execution — Specialized Costing (Project, Service, Intercompany) & Cost Governance (PA-158.3).)
- CTL-706: service cost built with loaded labor burden; actual collected to work order; variance analyzed monthly
Cross-references: - links to VS-12 (services), W544 (work order), VS-102 (comp/burden), W4627/W4634 (bundle allocation)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Under-burdened-labor risk**: Labor cost without benefits/burden understates service cost and overstates service margin; mitigated by the loaded-rate build (VS-102)
- **Subcontractor-cost-miss risk**: Subcontractor invoices not captured to the work order; mitigated by WBS/work-order-driven collection
System Touchpoints: - Service work order (W544); payroll/labor (VS-19.2/VS-102); subcontractor AP (VS-15); GL (VS-17.1)
Time Estimate: - ~per service type 2–4 hours; ~2–3 days/month service-cost variance

steps.activity: Build the service-cost standard: direct labor (loaded wage rate incl. benefits/burden per VS-102), subcontractor rate, vehicle/tool cost, and service overhead; allocate to the service work order (W544)
Collect actual service cost (technician timesheet, subcontractor invoice, vehicle/tool cost) to the work order; post service-cost variance (actual vs. standard)
Analyze service margin by service type/technician/region; feed into service pricing (VS-12) and the performance-obligation allocation for product+install bundles (W4627/W4634)

fields.Frequency: Per IC flow + quarterly TP review
fields.Volume: 5-entity group; warehousing/distribution fees, ecommerce fulfillment fees, rent (VS-97)

workflows.name: Intercompany Cost Transfer & Transfer-Pricing Cost Build

Automation Opportunity: - IC cost-transfer engine from serving-entity actual cost; auto-elimination on consolidation; TP-alignment dashboard
Controls: - CTL-706 (ensure controlled execution — Specialized Costing (Project, Service, Intercompany) & Cost Governance (PA-158.3).)
- CTL-706: IC markups arm's-length (TP-documented); cost base reconciled; eliminated on consolidation
Cross-references: - links to VS-72 (IC/shared services), VS-17.2 (consolidation/TP), W305/W612/W1299 (TP rules), VS-97 (rent)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Non-arm's-length risk**: IC markups not at arm's-length → BIR transfer-pricing exposure (VS-79/VS-17.2); mitigated by TP documentation and annual review
- **Cost-base distortion risk**: An inaccurate serving-entity cost base produces wrong IC fees; mitigated by the cost-base build and reconciliation
System Touchpoints: - Intercompany module (VS-72); transfer-pricing rules (W305/W612/W1299); GL (VS-17.1); consolidation (VS-17.2)
Time Estimate: - ~per IC flow 2–4 hours; ~3–5 days/quarter IC/TP accounting

steps.activity: Build the intercompany cost-transfer model: the cost-plus markup for BuildRight Logistics warehousing/distribution fees to Depot Inc., Digital Commerce per-order fulfillment fees, and Property Mgmt rent (at arm's-length transfer pricing per VS-17.2 W612/W1299)

Compute the cost base for each IC service (actual operating cost of the serving entity + agreed markup); post IC cost to the receiving entity and IC revenue to the serving entity; eliminate on consolidation (VS-17.2)
Validate transfer-pricing alignment (arm's-length) with TP documentation (VS-17.2 W1299/VS-72 W2594); adjust markups on the annual TP review and post IC reclass

fields.Participants: Merchandising (VS-45), Vendor Mgmt (VS-03), Controller, Revenue Accounting (VS-157)

Automation Opportunity: - Sell-through-triggered COGS + vendor-payable auto-post; cost-basis-to-settlement auto-reconcile
Controls: - CTL-706 (ensure controlled execution — Specialized Costing (Project, Service, Intercompany) & Cost Governance (PA-158.3).)
- CTL-706: consignment cost at sell-through (not receipt); principal/agent posture documented; reconciled to settlement monthly
Cross-references: - links to VS-45 (consignment/VMI), W543 (sell-through), W4628/W4629 (principal/recognition), VS-45.3 (settlement)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Cost-at-receipt error risk**: Booking consignment cost at receipt (as if purchased) mis-values inventory and cost; mitigated by the cost-at-sell-through rule
- **Settlement-reconcile risk**: Cost basis vs. vendor settlement mismatch distorts margin; mitigated by the monthly reconcile (W4629)
System Touchpoints: - Consignment/VMI module (VS-45); sell-through feed (W543); vendor settlement (VS-45.3); GL (VS-17.1); revenue (W4629)

steps.activity: Establish the consignment/VMI cost basis (vendor settlement price at sell-through, not at receipt — goods are vendor-owned per VS-45.1); confirm BuildRight as principal (gross) for the consumer sale (W4628)
At each sell-through (W543), post COGS at the consignment cost basis and the AP/vendor-payable at settlement; recognize revenue per W4629
Compute consignment/VMI margin (sell-through price − cost basis) by SKU/vendor; reconcile to the vendor settlement (VS-45.3); monitor commission/fee-type consignment where BuildRight is agent (net)

fields.Frequency: Monthly (+ weekly flash for volatile categories)

workflows.name: Cost-Accounting Calendar, Period Close & Cost Allocation Cycles

Automation Opportunity: - Dependency-aware cost-close orchestration; pre-sign-off exception gate
Controls: - CTL-706 (ensure controlled execution — Specialized Costing (Project, Service, Intercompany) & Cost Governance (PA-158.3).)
- CTL-706: cost calendar sequenced with dependencies; allocation cycles posted and reconciled; close validated before sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Cycle-sequence risk**: Allocation cycles run out of order (e.g., freight allocated before landed-cost finalized) → incorrect costs; mitigated by the sequenced calendar with dependencies
- **Late-exception risk**: Exceptions discovered after financial close require re-open; mitigated by pre-sign-off validation
System Touchpoints: - Close calendar (VS-17.1 W9A/W9B); allocation engine; variance ledgers; GL (VS-17.1)
Time Estimate: - ~5–7 days/period cost close (absorbed in the close cycle)

steps.activity: Maintain the cost-accounting calendar aligned to the fiscal close (W9A/W9B): standard-cost roll, landed-cost run, freight/duty allocation, overhead absorption, variance analysis, NRV review — sequenced with dependencies
Execute the cost-allocation cycles each period: freight/handling to SKU (W4652), overhead to product/service, labor to service/project (W4666), IC cost transfer (W4667); post and reconcile each cycle
Validate the cost close before financial-close sign-off: all variances posted, COGS reconciled (W4663), margin pack produced (W4661); resolve exceptions

fields.Participants: Master Data (VS-29), Merchandising (VS-01), Controller, Internal Audit (VS-21)
fields.Trigger: Cost-master change request; audit finding; governance review
fields.Volume: ~35K SKU cost records; vendor/contract cost data

workflows.name: Cost-Master Data Governance, Change-Control & Approval Matrix

Automation Opportunity: - Cost-change workflow with tiered approval + SoD; data-quality scorecard feed; change-audit-trail
Controls: - CTL-706: cost-master changes via governance with tiered approval and SoD; data-quality reviewed quarterly
Cross-references: - links to VS-29 (master data), W291 (data quality), W4649 (cost-master), VS-21 (audit), VS-88 (records)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Ungoverned-change risk**: A cost-master change bypassing governance (e.g., a buyer editing a cost) corrupts the cost layer; mitigated by the governance + SoD
- **Data-quality-decay risk**: Stale/incomplete cost data degrades margin analytics; mitigated by quarterly data-quality review
System Touchpoints: - Master data governance (VS-29); cost-master (W4649); data-quality monitoring (W291); audit trail (VS-88)

steps.activity: Govern cost-master data (cost elements, conversion factors, allocation bases, overhead rates, kit/BOM) through the master-data governance process (VS-29): request, validate, approve, post, audit-trail
Apply the cost-change approval matrix: standard-cost change tiered approval (Category Mgr → Controller → CFO by materiality); segregate those who request a cost change from those who approve and post
Review cost-master data quality quarterly (completeness, accuracy, timeliness); remediate data-quality issues and feed into the data-quality scorecard (VS-29 W291)

fields.Owner: Cost Accounting Manager / IT Finance Lead
fields.Trigger: ERP costing config change; new cost policy; audit remediation

workflows.name: Costing System Configuration: Cost-Sheet, Overhead Rates & GL Integration

Automation Opportunity: - Config-to-policy traceability dashboard; drift detection; automated config-test pack
Controls: - CTL-706 (ensure controlled execution — Specialized Costing (Project, Service, Intercompany) & Cost Governance (PA-158.3).)
- CTL-706: all costing config via change-control with Controller sign-off; config reconciled to policy semi-annually
Cross-references: - links to VS-27/VS-113 (IT/EA), VS-27.1 (change mgmt), W4649 (cost-master), W4646 (analog revenue config)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Config-drift risk**: Costing config diverges from documented policy over time → systematic cost errors; mitigated by periodic config review
- **Ungoverned-change risk**: Config change bypassing change-control breaks cost postings; mitigated by mandatory change-control and Controller sign-off
System Touchpoints: - Costing module config; GL integration (VS-17.1); change management (VS-27.1); EA standards (VS-113)

steps.activity: Configure and maintain the costing system: cost-sheet template per item class, overhead-absorption rates, allocation bases/engines, variance accounts, and GL integration (cost-to-GL mapping per entity)
Govern config changes through change-control (VS-27.1): test in non-prod, document, Controller sign-off, deploy; maintain a config-to-policy traceability matrix
Periodically review config for drift from documented cost policy (stale overhead rates, wrong allocation bases); reconcile config to the cost-master (W4649) and remediate

fields.Participants: Internal Audit (VS-21), Revenue Assurance (VS-118), IT Security (VS-27.3), Controller
fields.Trigger: Risk assessment; audit; control remediation; annual review

workflows.name: Cost-Accounting Internal Controls, Variance-Threshold & SoD Governance

Automation Opportunity: - SoD-conflict detection; manual-cost-adjustment log analytics; control-coverage report tied to cost-master
Controls: - CTL-706: documented control set mapped to internal-controls matrix; SoD enforced; audit trail retained 10 years; controls reviewed annually
Cross-references: - links to VS-21 (internal audit), VS-118 (revenue assurance), VS-27.3/VS-88 (security/records), W4657/W4660/W4663 (operating controls)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Cost-manipulation risk**: Manual cost-adjustment authority mis-used to manage margin; mitigated by SoD, restricted authority, and audit trail
- **Control-coverage gap risk**: A control missing for a new cost flow/category; mitigated by the annual control review tied to the cost-master
System Touchpoints: - Internal-controls matrix (VS-21); audit trail (VS-88); SoD roles (VS-27.3); ERP journal history

steps.activity: Maintain the cost-accounting control set: preventive (cost-change approval matrix W4670, config sign-off W4671, cost-at-sell-through rule W4668) and detective (variance-threshold investigation W4657/W4658/W4659, COGS reconcile W4663, NRV review W4660); map to the internal-controls matrix
Enforce segregation of duties: those who set standard cost, those who post cost journals, and those who reconcile/variance-investigate are separate; restrict manual cost-adjustment authority
Preserve the cost-change and variance audit trail for 10 years (BIR/audit); coordinate with Revenue Assurance (VS-118) on margin-leakage investigation spanning cost and revenue
